Everything that Rust could have been and wasn't, and for FREE. I played the roblox game that directly inspired Unturned religiously when I was younger. Unturned was obviously a much larger, much more ambitious version of that. The base-building mechanics in this game were better fleshed out and fun to play with. I loved how, even in its earliest state, Unturned had all sorts of systems and subsystems in place to play with. This wasn't just a zombie shooting gallery, you really had to be thoughtful about your ammo usage, food, armor, fuel, etc. It was really fun to play with friends cooperatively. With all of the updates the game has received since we last played, I would happily take a crack at playing again. The graphics, sound design, and music are surely *sparse*, but that adds to the indie charm of the game rather than detracting from it. For a small dev team, they focused on solid gameplay - good driving, shooting, etc. before making the game pretty, and I respect that. Fun title to playthrough for an afternoon or two, especially with such a competitive price!

Easily one of the best free to play games on Steam. This is a genre that has been over-done, but Unturned manages to be unique in it's own way. Kill zombies, gather resources, hunt animals, craft things and scavenge for items. That's all you do.

The beauty in Unturned stands in how simple it is, yet manages to be fun and quite graphically stunning. The developer team is just one single developer, and he's about 17 years old, that is something that should always be remembered, because not only does he update the game on a regular basis (about twice a week now), he has improved this game from an almost unplayable mess for older computers which was v2.0, to a polished and really smooth game v3.0 is.

Too PVP oriented, poorly made content, and full of racist children. That and the creator steals assets and mistreats his staff, doesn't abide by his own community standards. For that and more, I cannot genuinely defend the game. It was a neat concept full of potential in 2014, but in 2025 it aged like milk. Game play mechanics and graphics also differ between maps, which is confusing and disrupts the overall art style. Nelson is desperate to milk whatever more he can from the game through skin packs and stuff. Don't even buy Gold; it's just not worth it. I still enjoy the game on a rare occasion, but can't recommend anybody support it.

Personally I do not like multiplayer when im not playing with friends, but that is just me. Last time I played multiplayer it was mostly just kit servers.

A great F2P game, and a gold upgrade, although completely unnecessary, is pretty cheap, too. Like many games, it's a blast to play with friends.

What makes it great, though, is that Nelson actively listens to the community and puts out updates according to what we want. The community for this game itself is great, too, with so many new features coming from them.

Overall great game, and very well handled.
